issues.sym: A "Check Power Steering" message or warning light comes on and the steering suddenly turns very heavy, often at low speed or while parking. It may come and go before failing for good.
issues.why: The second-generation TSX uses electric power steering. Owners most often report a failed steering control module, and sometimes the steering rack and motor assembly itself.
issues.next: Treat heavy steering as a safety problem and drive gently until it is checked. Have a shop read the steering module codes; a used or rebuilt control module is often cheaper than a whole new rack.

issues.sym: You need to add a quart or more of oil between changes, the low-oil light comes on well before the next service, or the engine rattles briefly at startup when oil is low.
issues.why: Worn or sticking piston oil rings let oil get burned in the cylinders. Owners of 2009-2011 cars report dealers replacing piston rings, sometimes under extended coverage after an oil consumption test.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and never let the level run low, since low oil also wears the timing chain. Ask an Acura dealer to run an oil consumption test and check your VIN for any extended coverage.

issues.t: Passenger air bag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see or feel in normal driving. The danger shows up only in a crash.
issues.why: The Takata inflator in the front passenger air bag can break apart when the bag deploys and throw metal pieces into the cabin. Honda recalled these cars in several rounds.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls today and book the free replacement. Until it is done, keep the front passenger seat empty if you can.

issues.t: Replacement passenger air bag may be installed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign in normal driving.
issues.why: On some cars that already had the passenger inflator replaced, the new part was put in incorrectly, so the air bag may not open properly in a crash. Honda issued follow-up recalls to inspect and fix them.
issues.next: Even if your air bag was replaced before, check your VIN for open recalls and have the work re-inspected for free.

issues.sym: Harsh or late shifts, the engine revving between gears, a check engine light with transmission codes, or the car not wanting to move in Drive.
issues.why: The five-speed automatic in the first-generation TSX can wear internally. Owners report failures roughly between 80,000 and 130,000 miles that needed a rebuild or replacement.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition and have the codes read. Change the fluid with genuine Honda ATF on schedule; if it is already slipping, get a transmission diagnosis before it leaves you stranded.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak onto the exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, smoke from under the hood, or power steering fluid spots and a whining pump.
issues.why: A power steering hose can crack and drip fluid onto the hot exhaust pipe, which can cause smoke and, in rare cases, a fire under the hood. Honda recalled these cars to replace the hose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you see smoke or smell burning oil, pull over, shut the engine off and have the car checked before driving again.

issues.sym: Power steering fluid dripping near the front, a low fluid reservoir, steering that gets stiff or notchy, or a groan when you turn the wheel.
issues.why: The hydraulic steering rack's internal seals wear out, usually after 75,000 miles or so, and the rack starts leaking or losing assist.
issues.next: Top up with genuine Honda power steering fluid and have the leak traced. A leaking rack usually needs to be replaced, followed by a wheel alignment.

issues.t: Power steering pump whine or groan when cold
issues.sym: A whining or moaning noise right after a cold start that fades as the car warms up, often louder when turning the wheel.
issues.why: The power steering pump can pull in air through a worn inlet O-ring, or the pump itself wears. Owners report fixes ranging from a new O-ring and fluid flush to a replacement pump.
issues.next: Check the fluid level. Ask a shop to try the inexpensive O-ring and fluid flush first; replace the pump only if the noise continues or the steering gets heavy.

issues.t: Rattle for a few seconds after a cold start
issues.sym: A loud grinding or rattling noise from the engine for a second or two right after starting it cold, usually after the car has sat overnight.
issues.why: The variable valve timing (VTC) actuator on the camshaft wears and rattles until oil pressure builds. It is a well-known weak spot on this Honda 2.4L engine.
issues.next: It is not an emergency, but get it fixed. A worn actuator can lead to timing codes, and shops often check the timing chain and tensioner at the same time.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch and tensioner wear
issues.sym: A check engine light with camshaft timing codes (such as P0341), a rattle from the front of the engine, or rough running.
issues.why: As the 2.4L engine ages, the timing chain stretches and the tensioner and guides wear, especially if oil changes were stretched out or the oil ran low.
issues.next: Do not ignore timing codes. Have the chain stretch checked; replacing the chain, guides and tensioner before anything breaks is far cheaper than repairing engine damage.

issues.t: Engine can stall from a corroded engine computer (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Moisture can corrode the engine control unit, which can make the engine shut off without warning. Honda recalled these cars to inspect and replace the unit.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the engine has stalled while driving, have it checked before driving again.

issues.sym: The air conditioning suddenly blows warm air, sometimes after a clicking or grinding noise from the engine bay when the A/C is on.
issues.why: The A/C compressor clutch or the compressor itself fails on many TSXs, and a failed compressor can send debris through the system. Leaking A/C hoses are another common cause.
issues.next: Have the system checked with gauges before simply adding refrigerant. If the compressor has failed, the dryer and sometimes the condenser should be replaced with it so the new compressor does not fail early.

issues.sym: Squealing or grinding from the rear, or a shop telling you the rear pads are worn out at 20,000-30,000 miles, sometimes before the fronts.
issues.why: Many second-generation owners report the rear pads wearing out much sooner than expected, sometimes before the front pads. Rear caliper slides that stick can make it worse.
issues.next: Have the rear pads measured at every oil change. Replace pads before they reach the metal so you do not also need new rotors.

issues.sym: Grinding or a burning smell from one rear wheel, a wheel that is much hotter than the others after driving, or the car feeling like it is dragging.
issues.why: Rear caliper slide pins or pistons can corrode and seize, so the pad stays pressed against the rotor and wears both out quickly.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected soon. Replacing the stuck caliper, pads and rotors together, and lubricating the slide pins, fixes it.

issues.t: Some replacement accelerator pedals can bind (recall)
issues.sym: The gas pedal is slow to come back up, so the engine does not drop back to idle when you let off.
issues.why: A batch of replacement accelerator pedals sold as service parts could bind. Honda recalled cars that had one of these pedals installed.
issues.next: If your accelerator pedal has ever been replaced, check your VIN for open recalls. If the pedal sticks, shift to Neutral, brake firmly and pull over.

issues.t: Trunk wiring can short and kill rear lights (recall)
issues.sym: Blown fuses, and tail lights, back-up lights or the license plate light stop working.
issues.why: The wiring harness that runs into the trunk lid can be damaged as the lid opens and closes, causing shorts. Honda recalled these cars to repair the harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and walk around the car to confirm all rear lights work.

issues.sym: A battery or charging warning light, dim or flickering lights, a dead battery that keeps coming back, or a whining noise from the engine.
issues.why: The alternator is the most-reported part replaced on TSXs in owner surveys. On first-generation cars a leaking power steering pump can also drip onto the alternator and ruin it.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery again. If power steering fluid is leaking above the alternator, fix that leak too.

issues.sym: A single click or nothing at all when you turn the key, slow or grinding cranking, or the car starting only some of the time.
issues.why: The starter motor wears out, often past 100,000 miles. It is one of the most-reported repairs on the TSX.
issues.next: Have the battery and cables tested first. If they are good and the problem keeps happening, replace the starter before it leaves you stranded.

issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, rough idle, shaking, and loss of power, especially when accelerating.
issues.why: Individual ignition coils wear out with age and heat and stop firing their cylinder.
issues.next: Avoid hard driving with a flashing check engine light, since it can damage the catalytic converter. Have the misfire codes read and the bad coil replaced; replacing old spark plugs at the same time is common.

issues.sym: A check engine light, sometimes with slightly worse fuel economy or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: The upstream air-fuel ratio (oxygen) sensor ages and gives slow or wrong readings.
issues.next: Have the code read. Use a genuine or original-equipment sensor, since cheap ones often bring the light back.

issues.t: Water pump leak or bearing noise
issues.sym: Coolant drips or a sweet smell near the passenger side of the engine, a grinding or whirring noise at idle, or the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: The water pump bearing and seal wear out, usually past 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and temperature gauge. Replace the pump before it fails completely, and replace the accessory belt at the same time.

issues.sym: A clunk when shifting into Drive or Reverse or when you accelerate, and more vibration in the cabin at idle.
issues.why: The rubber engine and transmission mounts crack or collapse with age and mileage.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked while someone shifts between Drive and Reverse with the brake held. Worn mounts are not dangerous right away but they strain other parts.

issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, a wandering feel on the highway, a shimmy when braking, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The front compliance bushings and other rubber suspension bushings split as they age.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and get an alignment after any bushing or arm replacement.

issues.t: Clunk from worn sway bar links
issues.sym: A knock or rattle from the front or rear over small bumps, rough pavement or driveways.
issues.why: The small links and bushings that connect the anti-roll bars to the suspension wear out.
issues.next: This is a low-cost repair. Have the links checked during your next tire rotation.

issues.sym: One door, often the driver's, will not lock or unlock with the remote or switch, or it buzzes when you press the button.
issues.why: The small electric motor in the door lock actuator wears out. Owners report replacing them, sometimes more than once.
issues.next: Use the key or manual lock in the meantime and have the actuator replaced.

issues.t: Dashboard or navigation lights go dark
issues.sym: Gauge lights, the navigation screen backlight or switch lights on the center stack go dim or stop working.
issues.why: Bulbs and solder joints on the circuit boards behind the gauges and the navigation controls fail with age.
issues.next: It is mostly a nuisance. An electronics repair shop can often fix the board for less than a new part.

issues.sym: A squeak from the driver's seat and the seat shifting a little when you accelerate or brake.
issues.why: Play in the seat track lets the seat move and squeak.
issues.next: Have a dealer or shop inspect and tighten or replace the seat track.

issues.sym: On manual-transmission cars, a click or groan as you press the clutch pedal, often worse in warm weather.
issues.why: Dry plastic pivot parts at the clutch pedal, or a worn clutch master cylinder, make noise as the pedal moves.
issues.next: Lubricating the pedal pivots often fixes it. If the pedal feels soft or sticks, have the clutch master cylinder checked.

issues.t: Stability control (VSA) or ABS unit failure
issues.sym: The VSA, ABS and brake warning lights stay on, or braking feels uneven.
issues.why: The ABS/VSA control unit and pump (modulator) can fail internally. Owners report it as one of the more expensive TSX repairs.
issues.next: Have the codes read; low battery voltage or a wheel speed sensor can also set these lights. If the modulator itself has failed, a rebuilt unit can save money.

issues.t: Exhaust leak at the manifold or flex pipe
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound from under the hood, louder exhaust, or an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold, its joints and the flexible pipe crack or rust through with age.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected. Leaks near the engine can let fumes into the cabin, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Bluetooth phone connection drops or will not pair
issues.sym: Your phone will not pair, calls drop, or the hands-free system stops recognizing the phone.
issues.why: The hands-free link module and its software are dated and do not work well with many newer phones.
issues.next: Delete the pairing on both the car and the phone and try again. A dealer can check for software updates or a faulty module.
